# Properties

<!-- Generated by `mise run catalog:generate` from examples/catalog/: edit the entries, not this file. -->

Blender properties are declared as class annotations whose value is a call, `count: IntProperty()`, on a Property host
(a `PropertyGroup`, an `Operator`, a `Panel`'s ...). Python's typing spec says an annotation is a type, so a plain type
checker rejects the call and knows nothing of the attribute. The add-on typechecker reads it as Blender does: the
instance attribute has the property's Value type, and `bpy.types.Scene.x = IntProperty()` adds a Registered property
to every scene.

<a id="declaring"></a>
## Declaring properties

<a id="annotated-property"></a>
### A property declared as an annotation

**Handled** by [the add-on typechecker](by-handler.md#typechecker) · checked with Blender main, builtin stubs · `properties/annotated-property`

A Property host declares its properties as class annotations, `name: IntProperty(...)`. The annotation is a call,
which the typing spec rejects, but the checker reads it as a declaration: the attribute has the property's Value
type on every instance.

```python
from bpy.props import IntProperty
from bpy.types import PropertyGroup


class Settings(PropertyGroup):
    count: IntProperty(default=2, min=0)


assert_type(settings.count, int)
settings.count = "two"  # reported: invalid-assignment
```

- **What you see:** `settings.count` is `int`; ty reports [`invalid-assignment`](https://github.com/taway1450/ruff-blender/blob/blender/crates/ty/docs/rules.md#invalid-assignment) (error) on the line marked *reported*.
- **More:** [feature tests: properties](../../tests/typecheck/features/properties/README.md) · [source](../../examples/catalog/properties/annotated_property.py)
